methodology: BVPS compounding x exit P/B (insurer route)
methodology_note: Challenger is an APRA-regulated life insurer / annuity writer whose earnings are a spread on a regulated capital base, so the dcf-methods routing table sends it to the insurer row: compound book value per share at an Operating ROE path, net of dividends and buy-backs, discount dividends at the cost of equity, and capitalise terminal BVPS at a justified exit P/B. Operating cash flow (annuity premiums in, policy payments out) is not free cash flow; policyholder liabilities and the $8.4bn of interest-bearing liabilities/SPV debt are operating funding matched by investment assets, so no net debt is deducted from the equity value. Earnings basis is normalised/Operating NPAT (the company's own measure, $467.6m FY26) rather than statutory NPAT, which swings with investment experience (FY20 -$421m, FY26 +$505.6m).

inputs.share_count_basis: 683.8m ordinary shares issued and fully paid at 30 Jun 2026 (FY26 AR Note 13); 7.0m held in treasury for the employee Performance Plan roughly offset the 13.6m weighted potential plan shares, so held flat before buy-backs. Capital Notes 4 / CLC subordinated notes (115.7m weighted dilutive shares) convert only on an APRA trigger and are excluded. The CSV's 687.0 is the basic weighted-average count.
inputs.net_debt_note: Not deducted. total_debt (8,431.1) is interest-bearing liabilities + SPV funding backing the investment portfolio, and life contract liabilities are policyholder funds -- both are operating funding for a spread business, not a claim ahead of equity. Corporate facility $60m drawn of $250m is the only holdco debt and is immaterial.
inputs.last_fcf_basis: normalised NPAT FY26 (owner-earnings proxy for a life insurer; reported OCF of $1,904m is annuity flow, not distributable cash)
inputs.dividend_note: FY26 33.0c = 31.5c ordinary + 1.5c special, fully franked; $210.4m paid in cash. FY27 payout target 65-75% of Core Basic EPS (45-49c) = 29-37c.
inputs.sbc_source: CGF.AX_Annual_FY2026.txt:8253 share-based payments (cash-flow add-back); already expensed inside normalised NPAT, so no further deduction in an earnings/BVPS model. 5.2m shares were bought on market for employee schemes in FY26, neutralising plan dilution.
inputs.interest_income_note: Interest received $1,182.7m is the Life investment portfolio yield -- it IS the business, not surplus-cash income, so it is not stripped.
inputs.buyback_note: FY26: $87.6m paid, 7.9m shares cancelled (+1.9m bought not yet cancelled, $18.7m). Program upsized to $450m on 18 Aug 2026; ~$362m remains for FY27.
inputs.cost_of_equity_rationale: AUD flows, AUD rate: AU 10yr ~4.4% + 5.5% ERP x beta ~1.1 (spread/credit-sensitive life insurer with a 2018-20 drawdown from $13.6 to $4.3) = ~10.5% base; 10.0% bull / 11.5% bear vary the rate modestly with the risk in the flows already carried by the ROE and exit-P/B paths.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Not a WACC model: equity flows are discounted at the cost of equity (see cost_of_equity_rationale); policyholder and investment-portfolio funding is operating, not financing.
inputs.lease_treatment: Lease liabilities $30.5m are immaterial and inside operating expenses; no adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI nil at 30 Jun 2026 (3.8 at FY25).
inputs.notes: Model: BVPS compounding x exit P/B, the dcf-methods routing table's insurer row (same family as FRFHF). Reasons: (1) Challenger Life is an APRA-regulated annuity writer earning a spread on a regulated capital base, so value = book x (ROE vs CoE); (2) OCF is policyholder flow, FCF and EV/EBITDA are undefined; (3) net debt must not be deducted -- the $8.4bn total_debt is portfolio funding; (4) statutory NPAT is investment-experience noise, so ROE is set on the normalised/Operating basis the company guides to. Cross-check: the base terminal value implies ~11x FY31 EPS vs 15.2x FY26 normalised EPS today; the market's 1.75x P/B requires ~15-16% ROE at a 10.5% CoE, i.e. it is pricing the bull case. Price is the regular ASX close, not an after-hours print.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: guidance_operating_eps_cagr_low_end (FY27 medium-term target 8-10% Operating EPS CAGR); the BVPS model's own driver is ROE, not a growth rate
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-0.8% 3yr / +1.2% 5yr) diverges >30% from normalised NPAT CAGR (+8.7% / +10.9%): Challenger pays out or buys back essentially all normalised earnings, so book value is flat and per-share growth comes from a shrinking share count, not retained capital. Statutory EPS CAGRs (+20.5% 3yr / -3.6% 5yr) are investment-experience noise, not trend. FCF CAGRs are null: operating cash flow of a life insurer (annuity inflows less outflows) is not free cash flow.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue is not comparable across the FY2024 AASB 17 transition (two-line sum from FY24); the 5yr revenue CAGR straddles it and FY21 also carried an investment-gain rebound. Normalised NPAT 5yr CAGR starts at the FY21 COVID trough; the 10yr CAGR (2.6%) is the honest through-cycle figure.

base.description: Operating ROE 12.0% in FY27 rising to 12.5% (bottom of the new 12-14% through-the-cycle target; FY26 normalised ROE 11.6%, Life 13.2% with the corporate segment the drag). Dividends 47% of operating NPAT (= ~70% of Core Basic EPS, the mid-point of the new 65-75% payout target; FY26 declared 33c = 48% of normalised NPAT). The $362m balance of the $450m buy-back executes in FY27 at the current price, then $100m/yr of ongoing capital return as the July-2026 APRA longevity standards free capital. Exit P/B 1.30x = justified (ROE 12.5% - g 3%) / (CoE 10.5% - g 3%) = 1.27x, and in line with the FY22-FY24 trading range (1.17-1.24x) plus a modest premium for the ratings upgrade and less-cyclical capital regime; it implies ~11x exit P/E on FY31 EPS.
base.buyback_price_basis: FY27 at current price; FY28+ at opening BVPS x scenario exit P/B

bull.description: APRA capital reforms and the Calix Re / MS Primary reinsurance channel lift Operating ROE to the top of the 12-14% target by FY29; credit spreads normalise so the Life COE margin recovers from 3.06%; Fidante/Channel merger crystallises value and the $1.3bn excess capital is returned at $200m/yr after the current program. Exit P/B 1.60x = justified (14% - 3%)/(10% - 3%) = 1.57x, still below the FY18 2.1x growth-story peak. CoE 10.0%.
bull.buyback_price_basis: FY27 at current price; FY28+ at opening BVPS x scenario exit P/B

bear.description: Credit spreads stay tight and the COE margin compresses further; Fidante outflows persist; a negative investment-experience year (FY20: -$421m statutory) or the untested AdvILP capital models eat into book, taking Operating ROE to 9.5%. No capital return after the committed $450m program. Exit P/B 0.95x, between the FY20 trough (0.81x) and the FY21-FY23 range (1.0-1.2x). CoE 11.5%.
bear.buyback_price_basis: FY27 at current price; FY28+ at opening BVPS x scenario exit P/B

sensitivity.matrix_note: Base-case flows; rows are cost of equity (%), columns are exit P/B multiples (the terminal_growth_range key holds P/B values, not growth rates, for dashboard compatibility). Buy-back execution prices in FY28+ are held at the base exit P/B across the grid.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25. Bear held at 25% (not the 15% house default) because the earnings driver is a credit-spread margin already compressing (3.06%, -13bp), the FY27 Core Earnings framework and AdvILP capital models are untested, and statutory book can absorb a -$400m investment-experience year. Bull at 25% because the July-2026 APRA reform is a genuine structural tailwind and TAL paid ~$8.46 for 19.9%.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide: SBC is expensed inside normalised NPAT and the share count is not double-charged, so the house/street band collapses; band_position is null, not 0.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Challenger is valued as what it is: a regulated spread business whose worth is its equity base times the gap between the ROE it can earn on that base and the return shareholders require. At $10.36 the shares trade at 1.75x book and 15x normalised earnings, which a 10.5% cost of equity only justifies if Operating ROE reaches ~15-16% -- above the top of management's own 12-14% target. The base case (ROE 12.5%, 1.3x exit P/B) gives ~$7.5; the market is paying for the bull case of the APRA capital reform, and the 15% hurdle entry price is well below that.
key_risks_to_valuation: Exit P/B is the dominant input (terminal ~80% of value): each 0.15x is ~$0.70/share in the base case
COE margin compression from tight credit spreads flows straight into Operating ROE
Untested FY27 Core Earnings framework and AdvILP capital models; first-year comparability is poor
Statutory investment-experience losses can reduce book value in a single year (FY20 -$421m)
TAL/Dai-ichi 19.9% stake: takeover premium optionality on the upside, governance overhang on the downside -- neither is in the model
Fidante/Channel merger deconsolidates ~45% of Funds Management; ~$100m pre-tax gain is one-off and excluded

cross_checks.consensus_target_range: A$7.0 (Citi, Sell) to A$11.70; average ~A$9.4 (per Analysis.json)
